direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is bland and formulaic, as it just feels like a Jurassic Park cash grab and also does a poor job at mixing the A and B storylines; the direction on a microscale is bad, as all the interpersonal scenes feel campy in the A plot and just bad in the B plot; the storytelling is very bad, as they have an A and a B plot that are not connected at all, and when they try to converge storylines, it is just very forced; they build tension pretty well, but that would be hard to mess up in a Jurassic Park movie

performance.comments: Uses her experience as an action lead to carry this performance, as she does make bad material somewhat enjoyable
Really given nothing to work with as his character is barely given any screen time, despite him probably giving one of the best performances
Pretty unrecognizable, but his performance is memorable and I enjoyed it
Standard rich-action villain, and they make it even more formulaic with him being a part of an unnamed 'big pharma'
Genuinely don't understand why his character is in this movie and has no chemistry with the rest of the cast

cast.comments: The most campy and corny performances I have ever seen, as they are all shallow caricatures of what they were trying to convey; does not include child actors

story.comments: The concept is genuinely stupid, it's a shallow 'using the dinosaurs for evil big pharma'; the plot structure is very bad as there is an A and a B plot that are incredibly disjoint, with the former plot being genuinely useless; character writing is incredibly shallow and formulaic, as attested by the villain being an executive from a secret 'Big Pharma' company

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is so bad that I physically got mad at what they were saying; The humor is campy, so kind of funny how bad it is; The symbolism is so shallow that it hurts the message, it's a formulaic 'big pharma bad, open source the data' message; The foreshadowing makes the movie predictable and also creates no stakes

score.comments: Pretty good, and does a pretty good job incorporating the classic themes

cinematography.comments: What you would expect from a big-budget Jurassic Park movie

editing.comments: What you would expect from a big budget Jurassic Park movie; but some of the cuts are pretty bad

sound.comments: What you expect and want from a Jurassic Park movie is what helps make the dinosaurs realistic and scary

visual_effects.comments: What you expect and want from a Jurassic Park movie is what helps make the dinosaurs realistic and scary

production_design.comments: What you would expect from a Jurassic Park movie

review.pacing: Pacing is incredibly fast in the exposition as they breeze through this; Pacing is incredibly slow afterwards as this A/B plot is genuinely useless considering the B plot adds nothing to the story
review.climax: Climax is decently executed from an entertainment standpoint, but formulaic from a story standpoint
review.tone: Tone is Jurassic Park, but in a campier way
review.final_notes: They are going to keep making these movies because of how well they do at the box office because my theater was completely full;
review.overall: Overall, while the movie is very much on par with other Jurassic Parks in its advanced visual effects and sound, the movie is very bad from a direction and writing standpoint as it is obvious this is just a shallow cash grab; even though they need to end this franchise, they are going to keep making Jurassic Park movies until the wheels fall off because of how well this movie is doing at the box office
